CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Long wavelength upper level ridging is now expanding across eastern North America and will hold position through the end of the week and well into the weekend. Plan view perspective of relative humidity on isentropic surfaces supports a very subsaturated airmass throughout much of the troposphere amidst deep and persistent southwesterly flow this week. Forecast soundings are telling with strongly statically stable conditions from the surface through 18.0 kft agl. Virtually no precipitation potential exists for the next 5 days. Yet another long stretch of above normal temperatures with highs today and Wednesday in the 50s and highs during the end of the week eclipsing 60 degrees for many areas. NBM probabilistic data suggests a greater than 80% chance to reach 60 degrees Saturday for much of the area. These readings will be some 15 to 20 degrees above normal. Could see some minor br or haze around each of the dawn to daybreak periods with a lowered subsidence inversion into the surface. However, there is a persistent southwest gradient wind to contend with and the ground has not really cooled off to this point relative to climatology given the recent above normal temperatures. Thus, more of a period by period forecast with MOS guidance not overly pessimistic the next 48 hours. Models have been consistent in advertising precipitation potential with a deep trough system late Saturday and Sunday. All indications point to a period of good to strong lift across the area as a cold front tracks through area. Interesting note on the system is that ensemble data suggests that temperatures will not be all that cold following with forecasted surface temperature anomalies still suggesting above normal daytime temperatures at day 7 in the lower 40s. Will also offer that depending on the details of how the shortwave ejects through the area could be looking at breezy postfrontal conditions. && .MARINE... High pressure centered over Ohio this morning will drift southeast through tomorrow. Southwest return flow around the high will produce gusts of 15 to 25 knots over the central Great Lakes. A small craft advisory remains in effect today over Outer Saginaw Bay to Harbor Beach. A warm advection pattern will lead to a stable low level profile tonight, as 925 MB temps reach near 10 C. As a result, wind gusts on Wednesday are expected to fall short of 25 knots despite persistent southwest flow. Additionally, there will not be enough of an increase in low level moisture to support any rain activity through the workweek, as low pressure tracks well northwest Lower Michigan. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1240 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026 AVIATION... High pressure anchored over the Ohio River Valley will very slowly drop southeast towards the Central Appalachians over the next 24 to 48 hours. This will generally favor southwest flow across all terminals through Tuesday. Satellite imagery shows a pocket of thin high clouds moving over the area, thus have maintained BKN250 mentions into the overnight hours. Once these high clouds depart around 08Z, there remains some potential for previously mentioned shallow ground fog. However, VFR conditions remain the predominant signal in model guidance, so continued to hold off on including BR/FG in the TAFs. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * None. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...Small Craft Advisory until 10 PM EST this evening for LHZ421-441. Lake St Clair...None. Michigan waters of Lake Erie...None. && $$ DISCUSSION...CB MARINE.......SF AVIATION.....JA You can obtain your latest National Weather Service forecasts online at www.weather.gov/detroit.
